long_biography.plain_text:
Aker became Kjell Inge Røkke’s platform for active industrial ownership after he used capital from fisheries to secure control of the group. He had arrived in Seattle at 21 with no formal education or local network, worked in Alaska and built a global fisheries company. His holding company RGI became Aker’s largest shareholder in 1996 and later merged with it.

Røkke remains Aker’s chair and controlling owner, directing long-term investments through TRG. The portfolio spans energy, industrial technology, maritime services and marine biotechnology. He has also committed most of his wealth to philanthropy, supporting ocean science and environmental work through non-profit research and data organisations. His ocean programmes now combine research infrastructure with efforts to unlock industrial data for scientists and policymakers.
